relationships.description: The shared library sub-view groups configured component instances that it references but does not own, so an instance could be re-parented or survive removal of the sub-view definition.
relationships.evidence: The library sub-view's definition file lists component instance IDs by reference (e.g. a children array of refs to instances declared elsewhere) rather than declaring them inline.

relationships.description: The shared library sub-view owns the configured component instances that make up its assembly, so each instance exists only as part of that sub-view definition and is deleted with it.
relationships.evidence: The library sub-view's spec or JSX/template inlines the component instances with their prop values and render positions directly inside its own definition body.

relationships.description: The shared library sub-view adopts a reusable interaction recipe so its action controls follow the prescribed input modality and feedback sequence wherever the sub-view is embedded.
relationships.evidence: The library sub-view's definition names the action pattern by ID (e.g. actionPattern: confirm-then-toast) on its buttons or handlers, or imports the pattern's hook/utility.

relationships.description: The shared library sub-view declares a data binding that tells its embedded components which source (API, store, local storage, mock or static value) and field path supply their data.
relationships.evidence: The library sub-view's spec attaches a dataConfig entry naming the source and field path, or its component code consumes the binding declared in that DataConfig.

relationships.description: The shared library sub-view applies a declarative layout configuration that arranges its component instances with a given layout mode, grid tracks, spacing and alignment.
relationships.evidence: The library sub-view's definition references a layoutConfig ID, or its container element carries the grid/flex classes or styles defined by that LayoutConfig.

notes: aggregates and composes to componentinstance are mutually contradictory; the ComponentInstance definition ('placed inside a specific...LibrarySubView') implies composition, so aggregates looks redundant or wrong. uses to layoutconfig would read better as 'applies' (ux predicate for configuration/style), and uses to dataconfig arguably overlaps with 'binds-to'.
